THE FUNNIEST NIGERIAN FAMILY ON THE INTERNET W/ @Theoshosfamily | Lagos Meets London

The FUNNIEST NIGERIAN FAMILY ON THE INTERNET



This week on Lagos Meets London is all about family, Nigerian culture, and real life family dynamics …Trust us, it’s one you don’t want to miss …



We sat down with the funniest Nigerian family on the internet “The Osho Family” for an honest, funny, and insightful conversation about love, parenting, and navigating life between Nigerian roots,  London realities and being British Nigerian 



From how Mum and Dad found love, to raising Gen Z kids in today’s world (with a 19-year-old daughter leading the charge 👀), we dive into the highs, the challenges, and the moments that make their family dynamic so special.



We also get into:



Nigerian food debates 🍛 (you already know this got heated 😅)
Summer holidays and family traditions ☀️✈️
Life growing up in a Nigerian household vs London culture
Their rise to fame on social media and how they handle it
Parenting styles: discipline vs freedom in today’s generation
Funny family stories and real-life moments you’ll definitely relate to
What the future looks like for the Osho family


This episode is full of laughter, real talk, and moments that will feel very familiar if you grew up in a Nigerian home.



If you’ve ever had to translate for your parents, argue about food, or balance two cultures — this one’s for you.

The True Origin of the Yoruba People — The Story They Never Told Fully

The True Origin of the Yoruba People — The Story They Never Told Fully reveals a powerful Yoruba origin story where myth, memory, and identity intertwine to shape one of Africa’s most influential civilizations. In Yoruba tradition, origin is not just a story of migration, but a sacred narrative rooted in Ile-Ife—the spiritual center of existence—where figures like Oduduwa and Obatala are said to have shaped the beginning of life.

Through Yoruba history, oral tradition, royal lineages, archaeology, and cultural continuity, the Yoruba people preserved their beginnings across generations. From the remarkable bronze and terracotta works of Ife to the rise of powerful kingdoms like Oyo, Ijebu, and Ekiti, this African history documentary reveals a civilization that developed over time through shared systems of governance, belief, and identity.

This documentary explores Yoruba mythology, cosmology, and cultural memory, uncovering how stories of creation, kingship, and migration formed a complex and enduring identity—one that connects the physical world with the divine and ancestral realm in ancient Africa.

Discover how Yoruba civilization was shaped not by a single migration, but by emergence, continuity, and cultural depth, and why this origin story remains one of the most profound and debated histories in Africa.

What have you heard about the origin of the Yoruba people? Share your thoughts in the comments.

Heather Cox Richardson: The GOP No Longer Exists and It Looks Like the 1850s

Heather Cox Richardson, historian and author of the newsletter Letters from an American, joins Scott Galloway to discuss what the midterms could reveal about America’s political future—and why she sees echoes of the 1850s in today’s shifting coalitions.

She explains how concentrated wealth fuels political upheaval, why the backlash against billionaires could unite voters across party lines, and what Democrats would need to deliver if they win Congress. Plus, the case for a new era of trust busting, Elon Musk’s power, and why she’s watching JD Vance beyond Election Day.

Check out Letters from an American: https://heathercoxrichardson.substack.com/
